sections.h2: What does the Virginia homestead exemption protect?
sections.html:
Virginia's homestead exemption shields a householder's property from creditor process on a debt, up to dollar limits set in Va. Code 34-4. It is a debt-collection protection, and it is separate from the property tax relief programs that carry a similar name in conversation.

The statute gives every householder a choice of real and personal property to hold exempt, including money and debts owed to them. Part of the amount can be used on anything. A second layer applies only to property used as the principal residence of the householder or the householder's dependents.

Piece of the exemptionAmount in the statute
General exemption, any property you pick$5,000
General exemption if the householder is 65 or older$10,000
Principal residence of the householder or dependentsUp to $50,000 in value
Each dependent, when support is shownUp to $500
Veteran with a service-connected disability rated 40 percent or more (34-4.1)Additional $10,000

A dependent is someone who gets most support from the householder and does not have enough assets to support themselves, and no one can be a dependent of more than one householder.

Yes. The statute calls for an inflation adjustment on April 1, 2027, and every three years after that, using the change in the CPI-U over the most recent three-year period, rounded to the nearest $25.

Adjustments do not apply to bankruptcy cases begun before April 1, 2027. Because the amounts in your case depend on the filing date, check the current text of 34-4 on the Virginia legislature site before relying on a number from any summary, including this one.

sections.h2: How do you claim the exemption on real estate?
sections.html:
You claim it by signing a homestead deed, having it acknowledged and recording it like any other deed. The rules are in Va. Code 34-6, and nothing in the statute says it happens automatically.

  • The deed is recorded in the county or city where the real estate sits, or if the property is outside Virginia, where the householder lives in the Commonwealth.
  • It must declare the intention to claim the benefit and describe the property with reasonable certainty, with the householder's cash valuation.
  • The statute supplies a form that asks for the householder's name, dependents' names and ages, whether the veteran add-on is claimed, and any earlier homestead deeds.
  • In a federal bankruptcy case, the filed schedule of property claimed as exempt is enough to set property apart.

Personal property works the same way under 34-14, except the writing is recorded where the householder lives. The exemption can be set apart any time before the property is sold under creditor process or by a bankruptcy trustee. For garnished wages, the claim can be filed after the summons is served on the employer and on or before the return date.

sections.h2: Which debts can defeat a homestead claim?
sections.html:
Two categories are barred by 34-5: the purchase price of the property, and spousal or child support. The exemption also gives way to a waiver. Under 34-22, a person who writes a waiver on a bond, note or other instrument can have exempt property reached for that debt.

The wording that works is short: a statement that the signer waives the benefit of the exemption as to that obligation. A lender, in other words, may already have asked you to give up the protection when you borrowed.

Where a creditor has a mortgage, deed of trust or other lien on the property, the lien can be enforced first without exhausting other assets. The homestead also yields to that kind of secured claim, because the real estate was set apart subject to paramount encumbrances.

sections.h2: What happens to the exemption when you sell the house?
sections.html:
You may sell a homestead like any other real estate, and the buyer does not have to check how you use the money. Section 34-9 says exempt real estate can be sold, conveyed or exchanged, and the purchaser is not bound to see to the application of the purchase money.

  • If you reinvest the proceeds, the new property is exempt to the same extent as the old (34-20).
  • Property bought in an exchange or without a court order needs its own recorded writing, which must state where the funds came from.
  • Rents and profits from exempt property are exempt in the same manner (34-18).
  • If you stop being a householder or leave Virginia, the right to claim the exemption ends (34-24).
  • Amounts you set apart count against your maximum for eight years (34-21).

One more detail from 34-13: the part of the exemption tied to a principal residence can only be used on that kind of property and its proceeds, not on other assets. A creditor can also ask a court to reach any value over the limit if the property was worth more than the exemption when you set it apart (34-19).

sections.h2: How is this different from property tax relief?
sections.html:
Property tax relief lowers or defers the local real estate tax bill, and the rules come from a different part of the Code. The two most common programs are local and veteran based.

  • Under 58.1-3210, a locality may by ordinance exempt or defer real estate tax for a home that is the sole dwelling of an owner who is at least 65 or, if the ordinance says so, permanently and totally disabled.
  • The ordinance may limit the break to the increase in tax since the year the owner turned 65 or became disabled, or since the ordinance began, whichever is later.
  • Under 58.1-3219.5, a veteran rated 100 percent service-connected and permanently and totally disabled is exempt on a principal residence, plus up to one acre of land, for tax years beginning on or after January 1, 2011.
  • A surviving spouse keeps that exemption until remarriage and can move to a new residence without losing it.

Because the elderly and disabled program is a local choice, the age, income and net worth rules are set by your city or county.

sections.h2: Does the homestead exemption matter if you want to sell fast?
sections.html:
It can, when an owner is behind on bills and judgment creditors might reach the house. A homestead deed sets a floor of protected value, and any value above that can still be pursued, so the sale price and the liens on the title matter more than the exemption alone.

If you are weighing a quick sale, we can talk through your situation. For the legal side, an attorney who does debtor-creditor work in Virginia can tell you whether a homestead deed is worth recording before closing.

faqs.q: How much is the Virginia homestead exemption?
faqs.a: Under 34-4, a householder can protect $5,000 of chosen property ($10,000 at age 65 or older), plus up to $50,000 of value in a principal residence, plus up to $500 per dependent. Those amounts are set to be adjusted for inflation beginning April 1, 2027.

faqs.q: Do you have to file a homestead deed in Virginia?
faqs.a: Yes for real estate. You sign a writing, have it acknowledged and record it in the county or city where the property is located. In a bankruptcy case, the filed schedule of exemptions can serve as the setting-apart document.

faqs.q: Does the exemption protect against child support or a purchase money loan?
faqs.a: No. Section 34-5 bars the exemption against the purchase price of the property and against spousal or child support obligations.

faqs.q: Can you sell a house after setting it apart as a homestead?
faqs.a: Yes. Exempt real estate can be sold and the buyer need not watch how you apply the money. Proceeds you reinvest stay exempt to the same extent if the new property is documented properly.

faqs.q: Is the homestead exemption the same as the senior property tax break?
faqs.a: No. The homestead exemption protects property from creditors. The senior and disabled tax relief in 58.1-3210 is a local program that lowers or defers real estate tax, and each locality sets its own terms.

faqs.q: Does a veteran get any extra protection?
faqs.a: A veteran with a service-connected disability rated 40 percent or more gets an additional $10,000 creditor exemption under 34-4.1. A veteran rated 100 percent permanent and total can also qualify for the real property tax exemption in 58.1-3219.5.
